the 2', 3', and 4'-OHs of the terminal mannose unit of Manalpha(1->2)Manalpha are engaged in key interactions with domain A, and the 3'-OH of the terminal mannoses in Manalpha(1-->2)Manalpha and Manalpha(2-1-->6)Manalpha and the 2'-OH in Manalpha(2->1)Manalpha are involved in key interactions with the domain B.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3- and 4-hydroxyl groups of the reducing terminal residue are important for the interaction of CV-N with Man-9, which has been shown to be a potent inhibitor of HIV-1 infection.
the 4'-OH is involved in the binding of the Manalpha(1,2)-Manalpha(1,3)Manalpha trisaccharides, whereas the 3'-OH is not.
STD NMR can be used to determine the location and strength of the sugar-protein interactions in the CV-N-saccharide complexes.
